# Noctilucent Clouds: Earth's Twilight Jewels

After sunset paints the ground in darkness, the highest clouds in our atmosphere—floating 50 miles up at the edge of space—still catch the Sun's rays and glow an ethereal electric blue, creating a shimmering display invisible to the naked eye on most nights. These rare "noctilucent clouds," captured here over Sweden, are so delicate and high that they only become visible during summer twilight when sunlight sneaks under the horizon to illuminate them like nature's own neon signs.
